title: Entering the mosque
hook: O Allah, open the doors of Your mercy, and on leaving, of Your bounty (Muslim)
tomorrow: what do you say after a meal you didn't make?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the door of home: in Allah's name, I trust him, no power except by Allah. Packed, and still trusting. Today, a different door.

The shoe rack comes first: a wall of sneakers, sandals and work boots, and the small choice of which cubby is yours. Then socks on carpet, soft and a little cool. The street noise drops away behind the door. The Prophet ﷺ gave words for crossing that threshold, and for crossing it again on the way out, and they aren't the same words. One door opens onto mercy. The other opens onto bounty.
screen: `THE SHOE RACK.` → `SOCKS ON CARPET.` → `TWO DOORS, TWO LINES.`

segments.voice: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet ﷺ says: when one of you enters the mosque, let him say, O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy. And when he leaves: O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty. Mercy on the way in; bounty on the way out. Why the switch? Inside is where you come to be forgiven, quieted, held: rahma, mercy. Outside is the street, the job, the shift, the grocery run: fadl, bounty, the good things of the day you go out to earn. The Qur'an gives Friday the same rhythm. When the prayer is ended, it says, disperse in the land, and, in Pickthall's words, "seek of Allah's bounty." The mosque doesn't keep you. It hands you back to the world, asking for good in it. That's the detail to tell a friend tonight: a mosque has two doors, and you say something different at each. Tradition adds a custom of the body too: right foot first going in, left foot first coming out. So the whole thing is felt. Carpet, hush, a line said under the breath; then the warm air outside, the sound of traffic, and a different line. Mercy in, bounty out.
screen: `MERCY ON THE WAY IN.` · `BOUNTY ON THE WAY OUT.` · `DISPERSE, AND SEEK.` · `RIGHT FOOT IN, LEFT FOOT OUT.` · then, large: `MERCY IN, BOUNTY OUT.`

segments.voice: Find a doorway near you and walk through it slowly, right foot first, feeling the floor change under you. Pause on the other side. Then turn and walk back through, left foot first, the way some do leaving a mosque, and notice what shifts in you between going in and coming out.
Entering the mosque: two lines for one building. Open for me the doors of Your mercy, going in; I ask You of Your bounty, going out.
The line for the doorway: mercy in, bounty out, inside to be held and outside to go and earn. Two doors, walked.

howItsDone: Muslims entering a mosque may step in with the right foot and say the line asking for mercy; leaving, they step out with the left and ask for bounty.
